key_insight: Low-dimensional feature expectations enable computationally efficient concave utility reinforcement learning, with off-policy sample complexity matching standard RL’s dependence on target accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports reward maximization, imitation learning, and maximum-entropy exploration without directly estimating high-dimensional state-action occupancy measures.
method: Exploit known feature spaces in finite-horizon bilinear MDPs to estimate occupancy measures.
Use model-based optimistic concave utility policy optimization (OCUPO).
Reuse past trajectories through backward feature regression, with an extension to linear MDPs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical sample-complexity guarantees of Õ(ε⁻⁴) on-policy and Õ(ε⁻²) off-policy, up to controllable projection error; it reports no empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The off-policy guarantee requires suitable policy-class assumptions, while practical accuracy depends on controlling projection error.
paper_title: Provably Efficient Concave Utility Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation
